_meta.source: MOE pages on school types, specialised schools, special education and allied educators; SEAB on private candidates and access arrangements; SG Enable programmes
_meta.notes: EVERY ROW NEEDS A HUMAN AGAINST THE NAMED PAGE. This page names what exists and deliberately does not advise. This build has no business giving guidance on special educational needs, and a page that tried would be worse than no page, so each row says what a thing is, who it is for and how to ask for it, and stops there. The appliesHere field is the honest part: where this app's own planner does not fit a road, it says so in the same breath as what to use instead.

kinds.label: A government or government aided secondary school
kinds.sits: The Singapore Cambridge Secondary Education Certificate, with subjects at G1, G2 and G3.
kinds.leadsTo: Every destination this app plans for, from ITE to junior college.
kinds.note: This is the road the whole app assumes. Everything in Plan, Play and Act is built for it.

kinds.label: An independent school
kinds.examples: Schools that set their own fees and admit on their own terms.
kinds.sits: The SEC, and some also run an Integrated Programme alongside it.
kinds.leadsTo: The same destinations. The fee is the difference, and the Independent School Bursary exists for it.
kinds.note: The subject planner applies exactly as written. The money page has the fee and the bursary.

kinds.label: An Integrated Programme
kinds.examples: Six years through to the A Levels or the International Baccalaureate.
kinds.sits: No SEC. The final exam comes at eighteen instead of sixteen.
kinds.leadsTo: University, mostly, and every other route stays open to somebody who leaves the programme.
kinds.note: The subject planner assumes an exam at sixteen, so its arithmetic does not apply. Everything about work, money, wants and the years to twenty does.

kinds.label: A specialised independent school
kinds.examples: NUS High School of Mathematics and Science, School of the Arts, Singapore Sports School, School of Science and Technology.
kinds.sits: Depends on the school. Its own diploma, the International Baccalaureate, or the SEC.
kinds.leadsTo: Universities here and abroad, conservatoires, sport, and every route in this app.
kinds.note: Where the school runs its own diploma there is no SEC to plan, so use the work, money and wants pages and ask the school about its own progression.

kinds.label: A specialised school
kinds.examples: NorthLight School, Assumption Pathway School, Crest Secondary, Spectra Secondary.
kinds.sits: The ITE Skills Certificate, with hands on learning through the whole programme.
kinds.leadsTo: Nitec at ITE, then Higher Nitec, then everything the ITE road reaches, which is a lot.
kinds.note: The ITE Skills Certificate is a real qualification and a real entry to Nitec, and this app's planner does not model it. The work page and the ITE road do apply, in full.

kinds.label: A special education school
kinds.examples: Government funded schools run by social service agencies, for students up to eighteen.
kinds.sits: A curriculum set for the student, which may include national exams or may not.
kinds.leadsTo: Open or supported employment, further training including ITE for some students, and day activity centres.
kinds.note: This app does not model this road and should not pretend to. Transition planning inside the school is the real instrument, and SG Enable runs the school to work programmes.

kinds.label: Not in a mainstream school right now
kinds.examples: Private candidates, home education, students returning after time away.
kinds.sits: The SEC as a private candidate, or another qualification.
kinds.leadsTo: The same destinations, on the same published criteria as anybody else.
kinds.note: The admission arithmetic applies as published. Registration as a private candidate goes through SEAB rather than through a school.

support.label: Access arrangements for exams
support.what: Extra time, a reader, a scribe, a separate room, enlarged papers, and others, for national exams and school exams.
support.who: Students with a diagnosed condition that affects how they can sit a paper.
support.howToGet: Applied for through the school, well in advance. The school knows the evidence needed and the deadline.
support.note: This is not an advantage and it is not a favour. It removes something that was measuring the wrong thing.

support.label: The Allied Educator for learning and behavioural support
support.what: A trained member of staff in the school who works with students who need a different approach, and with their teachers.
support.who: Anybody the school identifies, and anybody whose family asks.
support.howToGet: Ask the form teacher who the school's Allied Educator is. Most schools have one.
support.note: Often the person who knows most about how a particular student learns, and the least asked for by name.

support.label: Transition planning
support.what: Structured planning for what happens after school, started years before it happens, in special education schools.
support.who: Students in special education schools, from around thirteen.
support.howToGet: It is part of the school's programme. The family is meant to be in the room for it.
support.note: The real version of what this app does, run by people who know the student.

support.label: SG Enable
support.what: The agency for disability in Singapore. School to work programmes, training, employment support and funding.
support.who: Students and adults with disabilities, and their families.
support.howToGet: Directly, and the school can make the introduction.
support.note: Start earlier than feels necessary. The school to work programmes have intakes and places.

support.label: The ECG counsellor, for this in particular
support.what: The person in the school whose job is exactly the join between a student's situation and what comes next.
support.who: Every student in a mainstream secondary school has one.
support.howToGet: Book a slot. The room is usually empty at lunch.
support.note: Where this app stops, that conversation starts. Nothing on these pages replaces it.
